docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
FusionFix adds new options to the in-game menu that can be easily changed in real time and it also improves some of the games original options as well.

GTA IV's menus are quite limited, so the mod can only add so much to the menus before they run out of space. So a few options might not be in ideal locations.

The options below are labelled whether they're New or Improved.

docs.title: FOV (New)
docs.text:
Changes the field-of-view.

Before After

docs.title: Language (New)
docs.text:
Changes the language in-game. This was in previous GTA IV versions, but Rockstar removed it in The Complete Edition and instead tied it to your language settings in the Rockstar Games Launcher.

Before After

docs.title: Definition (Improved)
docs.text:
This alters the behaviour of the blur used to hide screen-door transparency artifacts on objects fading. Settings this to On will use the new Fusion Fix implementation which is similar to GTA V, this means the blur effect will only apply to objects which contain these artifacts (sharpest and cleanest image for GTA IV possible out of all the platforms). Setting this to Off will apply the blur effect to the entire screen, similar to Xbox 360.

This option was in the original game, but it's basically been completely reworked in Fusion Fix. See the dedicated Fusion Fix Definition section for more information.

Before After

docs.title: Console Gamma (New)
docs.text:
This enables the gamma curve from the Xbox 360 version of GTA IV. This makes the game look less washed out and more contrasty.

Before After

docs.title: Console Auto Exposure (New)
docs.text:
This enables the auto exposure effect seen on the console versions of GTA IV. This is intended to simulate your eyes adjusting to different light levels, e.g. looking at the sun and then looking down at the ground, the ground will appear dark for a second until your eyes adjust.

Before After

docs.title: Motion Blur (New)
docs.text:
This allows you to enable/disable/change the intensity of the motion blur seen when driving fast in vehicles.

In the vanilla game, motion blur is tied to the original Defintion option and the intensity of the effect was weaker at higher frame rates.

Before After

docs.title: Depth of Field (New)
docs.text:
This allows you to enable/disable/change the intensity of the depth of field effect (objects blurred that are out of focus/in the distance).

Keep in mind, depth of field is also controlled by the games time cycle (timecyc.dat file). Certain weathers/times of day won't present any depth of field in the vanilla game and The Ballad of Gay Tony's time cycle has depth of field disabled entirely.

In the vanilla game, depth of field is tied to the original Defintion option and the intensity of the effect didn't scale correctly beyond 720p (blur got weaker at higher resolutions).

Before After

docs.title: Tree Lighting (New)
docs.text:
This is a WIP.

Before After

docs.title: Tree Alpha (New)
docs.text:
This is a WIP.

Before After

docs.title: Bloom (New)
docs.text:
This allows you to enable or disable the bloom effect. Fusion Fix also rewrites the code for bloom, fixing issues such as bloom getting less intense at higher resolutions.

Before After

docs.title: Screen Filter (New)
docs.text:
This allows you to switch between the three screen filters used in each episode of GTA IV or disable them entirely. If left to Default, the game will use the screen filter intended for that episode.

Before After

docs.title: Distant Lights (New)
docs.text: This allows you to switch between the games default distant lights or the Project 2DFX lights, which is integrated directly into Fusion Fix.

docs.title: FPS Limiter (New)
docs.text: This allows you to limit the frame rate in-game to several pre-set values or to a custom value set in GTAIV.EFLC.FusionFix.ini.

docs.title: Anti-Aliasing (New)
docs.text: This allows you to enable two forms of anti-aliasing, SMAA or FXAA.

docs.title: Volumetric Fog (New)
docs.text:
This allows you to enable or disable the new volumetric fog in Fusion Fix. The original game fog moves with the camera position and when the player is up high, you can see the water cut off at the horizon.

Fusion Fix's volumetric fog no longer moves with the camera position, it increases the farclip (draw distance) to 4500 meters, the fog itself blends in with the bottom sky colour seamlessly and the horizon cutting off is no longer visible.

docs.title: Sun Shafts (New)
docs.text:
This allows you to enable or disable the new sun shaft effect in Fusion Fix. The original games sun is pretty effectless when compared to every other GTA title, but this options adds god rays coming from the sun which looks excellent.

docs.title: Extended Sunlight Reach (New)
docs.text:
This option allows you to enable or disable Fusion Fix's improved sun lighting.

In GTA IV, how much a surface is lit is determined by the angle between the direction it is facing and the direction of the sun. It can be up to 90 degrees, but vanilla GTA IV clamps it at 75 degrees. Enabling this option allows it to reach 90 degrees.

docs.title: Tone Mapping (New)
docs.text:
This option allows you to enable or disable tone mapping introduced by Fusion Fix.

This stops highlights from getting blown out and clipping.

You can change the tone map operator by replacing XX in YY, more operators can be found here.

docs.title: Ambient Occlusion (New)
docs.text:
This allows you to enable or disable the new ambient occlusion effect in Fusion Fix.

Ambient occlusion simulates light being blocked by objects, giving objects much more depth than before.

docs.title: Shadow Filter (New)
docs.text:
This allows you to switch between various shadow filters.

Fusion Fix includes a CHSS filter which makes shadows sharper when they're near the object casting the shadow and softer when the shadow is further away from the object casting the shadow.

docs.title: What is it?
docs.text:
Modding isn't for everyone. Some people just want to play the best version of thier favourite games without learning how to install every type of mod possible, even if it is easy.

TJGM's Drag n' Drop Archive is a modpack for Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition that is aimed at giving new players the best experience possible quickly, so they can jump right in and play.

This modpack contains four essential mods that give you the best GTA IV experience on ANY platform. Bug fixes, improved controls, new quality-of-life features, improved graphics, restored cut music and much more.

Before you download and install the modpack, PLEASE read the warnings below.

docs.title: What this modpack contains
docs.text:
Down below you'll find each mod in the modpack, the mod versions in the current pack and a quick description of what each mod does.

  • Console Visuals (v2.1) - Brings console assets to PC. Modpack only includes console vegetation and console fences, as they're assets which are definitively better than the PC assets, the rest is subjective.
  • Fusion Fix (v5.0.0-hotfix5) - Adds many new faithful graphical effects, a TON of quality-of-life features which brings the game up to a more modern standard, fixes hundreds of bugs including high-FPS bugs, adds many new options and overall just massively improves the experience.
  • Higher Resolution Miscellaneous Pack (v2.0) - Faithfully sources or recreates high definition textures for several areas on the map, including ground rubbish, props, interiors, minigame textures and more.
  • Higher Resolution Vehicle Pack (v2.4) - Faithfully sources, recreates and improves all vehicle textures across the game, including interiors, tyres, vinyls, dirt textures, etc... This mod also includes unique license plates for every individual vehicle, as well as special plates for police vehicles, taxis and motorbikes.
  • Radio Restoration (23-05-2025) - Restores cut music. Modpack only includes basic configuration.
  • Various Fixes (v2.0 - Hotfix) - Fixes a huge number of texture issues, prop placement mistakes and other problems and inconsistencies throughout GTA IV's map.

docs.title: Download and Installation
docs.text:
1. Download the latest TJGM's Drag n' Drop Archive for GTA IV vX.Y.Z from the official TJGM's Drag n' Drop Archive for GTA IV release page (found under Assets).
  2. Open the archive you just downloaded and then copy and paste everything from the archive into your game folder where GTAIV.exe is located.

Tip

If you're not sure how to find your game folder...

  • Steam: You can find it by right clicking on Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition in your Steam library, going to Manage and then clicking Browse Local Files. The GTAIV folder is where GTAIV.exe is located.

  • Rockstar Games Launcher: You can find it by clicking on Settings in the Rockstar Games Launcher, click Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition in your installed games list, find View installation folder and then click Open next to it. The GTAIV folder is where GTAIV.exe is located.

  • Steam Deck: Launch the Steam application while on your desktop, locate Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition in your Steam Library, press the Left Trigger on the game to open the context menu, go to Manage and then click Browse Local Files. The GTAIV folder is where GTAIV.exe is located.

For Steam Deck/Wine/Proton you also need to do the following...

  1. Launch the Steam application while on your desktop, locate Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition in your Steam Library, right click or press the Left Trigger on the game to open the context menu and press left click or Right Trigger on Properties...
  2. In General, go to Launch Options and in the text box enter WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" %command%"
